utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. Most of the documents that were shown to me refer to operatives whom I know personally. I, as head of the analysis department, talk to them frequently in order to assess the veracity or reliability of information and in order to prepare further activities for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to take you to paragraph 7 of your statement. And may that be displayed in Sanction. It refers to an operation called Krug, or circle, in the mid-1990s onwards and which you say relied on all of the sources of information described before, human intelligence, electronic surveillance, and media reports. What was the purpose of this Operation Krug and who authorised it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I can say quite a lot about this, given that I personally drafted a proposal to initiate the Operation Krug, defining the objectives and tasks for the State Security Service. The need for this operation arose once the extremist and terrorist activity in Kosovo and Metohija was on the rise. That was in mid-1996. Based on the information we had during that period of time, we learned about some data which very reliably indicated that an organised work of an illegal organisation stood behind these activities, and that organisation was the LPK, People's Movement of Kosovo. Based on that, I drafted a proposal to initiate this operative action, in order to locate, monitor, and put an end to such type of activities. And this action was to be conducted in -- in Pristina and it was to be monitored in all other centres. As for the decision to initiate this action, it was taken in Belgrade by the Minister of the Interior. So we gave a proposal, and the Minister of the Interior of Serbia passed the decision to initiate this operative action, which was targeted -- or rather, which targeted the activities of the LPK, People's Movement of Kosovo, and the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was in charge of it in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: This operative action -- rather, this operation fell under the responsibility of the chief of the RDB in Kosovo and Metohija. At that person -- at that time, that position was held by David Gajic. And after him, in late '98, Milosav Vilotic was appointed to that position. The immediate superior -- or rather, the person who stood between me and them was Milan Lakovic, chief of the security centre in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turning to paragraph 10 of your statement, which we'll also display in -- in Sanction, you say that "Virtually every report and written document concerning terrorist activities of the KLA in the Dukagjin operational zone in 1998 contains mention of Ramush Haradinaj or a member of his family, in particular, Daut or Nasim." Was the information you're referring to there gathered as part of Operation Krug? Yes? No? Maybe?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear the interpretation. The interpreters are saying that they could not hear the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Re please come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Paragraph 10, the first line. Just read that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: The first ten --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to yourself. Was the information referred to there gathered as part of Operation Krug?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You then refer to telephone conversations and electronic surveillance of Ramush Haradinaj and Lahi Brahimaj and close associates. What happened to the transcripts or tapes of these conversations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I can't give you an answer to that question. I know that these documents and transcripts were made, that there are recordings of these conversations, and as to where they are located, I wouldn't be able to say. I think you need to direct that question to the authorities in Belgrade and ask them where this documentation is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you believe them still to exist?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I am convinced that a large portion of these documents exists. I know that that in the eve of the bombing we pulled out quite a lot of documents from Kosovo and Metohija and we moved them to safe areas in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please move to paragraph 18 of your statement, which you refer to an anthology of KLA documents in a book edited by Gafurr Elsani. You refer to the foreword of the book being written by one Emrush Dzemailji, who wrote that KLA was part of the LPK's project. Who was Emrush Dzemailji?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Emrush Dzemailji at that point was the chairman of the People's Movement for the Republic of Kosovo. He is one of the leading members of these illegal organisations that were active in early 1980s in Kosovo and Metohija. After the last meeting that he had in March in Tirana, the meeting with the Albanian immigration, where they promoted KLA, he moved to Kosovo and Metohija and from that time until the end, he was in the staff of Ramush Haradinaj in Glodjane. He had a pseudonym for his protection and he also had people protecting him. Even nowadays he's a highly placed official of that organisation, the People's Movement of -- for Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How well-placed was he, according to what you know about him and his activities, to provide an assessment about the documents in that book?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think the question as phrased calls for speculation and is outside the knowledge of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I press the question. I'm asking the witness for his information about Mr. Dzemailji, and based upon that, how well placed Mr. Dzemailji would have been according to what the witness knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as you formulate it now, it starts at least more factual than the previous formulation. Please proceed on the basis of the second formulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: This is no speculation whatsoever. This is a book published by the People's Movement for Kosovo, published in Switzerland in March of 1998. In this book, they publish in the chronological order the documentation of the KLA and the People's Movement for Kosovo, depicting the development of that organisation and the terrorist KLA. This man was the chairman of the People's Movement for Kosovo. He was the most influential member of that party. And the KLA is their military wing or military project. He arrived in Glodjane from Tirana, where he attended a gathering promoting the KLA. After arriving in Glodjane, he spent a long time in the staff of Ramush Haradinaj under a pseudonym in Glodjane. He wasn't alone there. There were many other members of that organisation. For example, Hajdin Abazi, who was one of the key members of the NPOK. He had a pseudonym under which he stayed near Djakovica. As for Dzemailji, from the very beginning of his stay in Glodjane, he had a lot of influence with Haradinaj and enabled Haradinaj to stay in that area and to keep the position that he kept there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you'd like to know on what basis the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No -- yes, I think -- I think if I may say so, it's extremely important to keep a clear distinction between factual information and opinion evidence. And it is inevitable - and we see it in the 92 ter statement in the passages that the Trial Chamber has already directed to be removed from it - but it is inevitable that if open questions are asked, we will find ourselves drifting, as we do there, into a mixture of fact and opinion. And really, with respect, the matter needs to be built up, if it is going to be built up in stages. I don't, at this particular stage, ask Mr. Re to go back over the question that he's asked and retrace his steps. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In broad terms, if we are to avoid opinion evidence from this witness, it needs to be simple questions with a factual basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, it would certainly prevent objections in the near future if you'd take the witness step by step and focus as much as possible on facts, to start with. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your information about Mr. Dzemailji's influence within the LPK and KLA?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact that Emrush Dzemailji was the president of the People's Movement for Kosovo, which was the organisation that founded the KLA. It is a fact that after a meeting in Tirana chaired by him personally he moved over to the territory of Kosovo. It is a fact that Emrush Dzemailji --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that your response to my request to -- to have facts. But starting a sentence by says that it is a fact doesn't make such a matter of fact. I would say, first of all - and that's something you could tell us from your own observation - is from whom you learned about these events. Because that's what you experienced yourself. I take it that you were not with this person when he came from Tirana. So we'd like to -- first of all, to know about your source of information on what you just told us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, do you want me only to mention the period as of which Emrush Dzemailji was at the headquarters in Glodjane; that is, towards the end of March 1998? Or do you want me to address the genesis of the movement and the role of Emrush Dzemailji in all of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not seeking that. I'm just referring to your answer. You said: "It is a fact that Emrush Dzemailji was the president of the People's Movement for Kosovo." How did you learn that? Have you seen documents he signed? Is it -- did he appear on television as such? I mean, how do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We knew because we were in possession of certain documents which came from the meetings held by the organisation in the preceding period. We also learnt through our live sources that we had in Switzerland and Germany that were in close contact with him. And we also learned from some positions expressed by Emrush Dzemailji in public as well as about the documents that were published in the Albanian media in Kosovo and abroad. And when talking about the media, none of the things were ever denied by either Emrush Dzemailji or anyone else at that time or nowadays, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps, Mr. Re, the same for the next fact the witness presented, that he moved to the territory of Kosovo after a meeting he chaired in Tirana. How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Albanian television in Tirana broadcast in the evening hours of that day that there was a meeting held in Tirana where Emrush Dzemailji was and where he addressed those present. There were several other members of the presidency as well, including Iber Demaj [phoen], who was a person from the area of Pec. At that meeting, they familiarised the media with the situation in Kosovo and Metohija and the role that the NPK had and was supposed to play in the period following that. Through a person who was present at the press conference, we were told that a significant portion of the leadership of that organisation towards end March and early April illegally crossed into Kosovo and Metohija and took part in KLA activities in the field directly. I mentioned already Emrush Dzemailji, and I think I also mentioned Hajdin Abazi. That person was one of the persons of the NPK that used a fake name and a pseudonym. In Munich, he was Lym Haxhiu [phoen]. The public knows about that person as the person who under that fake name and pseudonym welcomed a high delegation from the United States, including Mr. Holbrooke and so on and so forth. Then some other people went further afield into the territory of Kosovo; namely, Adem Grabovci who was also in the area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. I was mainly trying to find out what the source of your knowledge was in relation to this person that, after having chaired a meeting in Tirana to -- going to Kosovo, rather than to have more details about that. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt again. Very often - and we see it in the last series of questions and answers - this witness will refer to information from live sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, I'm assuming when he uses an expression of that kind that it is a source that he is not willing to name, and therefore I don't propose on each occasion to stand up and seek identification of the source, because obviously an anonymous source of information is a matter which is going inevitably to weigh in the Trial Chamber's evaluation of what weight can be attached to any information provided. But -- but may I simply adopt the position that unless the witness volunteers the name of his source, we are assuming it is a source that he is unwilling to name for the purposes of these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- let's ask the witness. When you're saying that you learned something from a source which you do not name, is that because you are not willing to give that name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you. It had to do with the journalist present. But even before that, Your Honour, I had said that that news was broadcast on television.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But from now on, if you don't give the name of a source as someone who gave the information, you are invited to either spontaneously give the name of that person or, if you don't, we understand that you have reasons to prefer not to give that name. That's how we'll understand your testimony. Please proceed, Mr. Re. Well, I'm looking at the clock. Perhaps it would be the suitable moment for the break. May I invite the parties, also the Defence -- I do understand that the interventions until now were not without reason. Nevertheless, I would like to urge you to -- to keep them as limited as possible, because it really interrupts the flow of evidence Mr. Re wanted to elicit. And I'll try to improve as well, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before you break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In terms of the attachments to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we get -- can the registry allocate numbers to each of these? They've all got 65 ter numbers. I obviously can't take the witness through every one, and they're going to go out of sync, because we want to argue at one point the admissibility of some of them. Some of them aren't objected to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest, as a matter of fact, that for the time being that we work on the basis of the annexes as we find them here. Because we soon will get at a point where you might argue that all of them are admissible evidence and where the Defence might take a different position. We'll then decide. If the Defence were to say, "No, Mr. Re, we're fine with all of the documents." They have said they're not. Then perhaps they change their mind. Then we could, perhaps, assign one exhibit number, if we are making a selection or if you are making a selection or the Chamber will make a selection, then we might assign individual numbers to individual documents. So for the time being, I would prefer to work on the basis of these numbers, attachment number, because that's also easier to find.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, I understand, but the difficulty is that I've already referred to one -- I think I got a number P932 or something. So one's in. It's already out of sync. I want to refer to maybe 20 or 30 or so individually. But that means they're going to get numbers out of order, which means it's going -- it's going to be difficult to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I do understand that the order is not without importance for you. Mr. Registrar, whenever we -- whenever Mr. Re indicates that he would like to have a document marked for identification, could you assign it a number and then later on we'll decide on whether it will be tendered, whether it will be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking is can they all be given a -- a marked number, maybe during the break, so they'll all be in sync and then we could argue the admissibility afterwards. That way they would keep them in the same order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All the of the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole series?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yeah, one, two, three, four, five, whatever. 932, three, four, five, six, et cetera, and then that we could argue whether they go in or not afterwards, and that way they all remain in the same order rather than going backwards and forwards, and I've referred to some but not others and some have got numbers and some haven't. But that's all I'm asking, just to keep it neat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would that be something you could do? Then Mr. Registrar will provide you with the numbers, irrespective of what will happen with the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, mindful of -- of Your Honours' comments about interruptions, I obviously don't know which documents it is that Mr. Re intends to take the witness to, but there's quite a lot of them. I am entirely in the Trial Chamber's hands, but we object, as Your Honour knows, not simply to the annexes but to the summary from the witness of the contents of the annexes. Now, I don't wish to take time every time Mr. Re moves to place on the record, if that is what he's intending to do, the content of a document through the witness in rising to my feet to object, but it does seem to me, with respect, that insofar as the 92 ter statement and then the oral testimony, is designed simply to bring together and summarise the contents of annexes the admissibility of which is still in dispute, then time might better be spent, rather than having that put on the oral record and objections taken, time might better be spent in dealing with other matters. In other words, I'm anxious to avoid a situation where I'm bobbing up and down to object to oral testimony, which is -- if you like, in lieu of -- lieu of admitting documents, the admissibility of which is the subject of firm objection and an outstanding ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It, of course, very much depends on how the questions are put.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, summarising a document could start with: Have you seen this document? Have you drafted this document? Signed this document? Do you know the author of this document? Which, of course, adds already quite a bit to the annexes and -- and might change the situation. I think Mr. Re is perfectly aware of how he can avoid what he can expect --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on the basis of what Mr. Emmerson just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, entirely understandably, asked for objections to be kept to a minimum, but that entirely depends upon the way in which the evidence is elicited in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re is aware of that. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Only and ever so briefly, there still remains, as I'm sure Mr. Re is aware, the procedural issue with regard to the admission of any of these documents as it relates to 65 ter requirements, which have been raised in the motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Mr. Re is -- so we don't lose sight of the procedural issue. Also if while I'm on my feet, if I could quite quickly -- I don't know whether the gentleman would be willing to, but if so, we could get a copy of the proposal to initiate Krug, that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if he has it. Do you -- it's still -- is still the proposal to initiate the Operation Krug in your possession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It is in the archives of the RDB. However, I believe you can get both the proposal and the decision from our authorities easily, both the proposal drafted by me and the decision signed in Belgrade and that was forwarded to Kosovo permitting further activities concerning Operation Krug. Therefore, the proposal and the decision, I believe that is the title of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, I do not know whether it's already somewhere in your documentation; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we have the practical problem of the witness supposed not to further discuss matters with you or with anyone else. At the same time, if the parties could come up with a proposal on how to obtain this document in a way acceptable to both parties and then preferably, I take it, as soon as possible, the Chamber would consider to follow such a suggestion. We have a break and we'll resume at ten minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, please proceed.. But perhaps I'll first ask whether there are any suggestions on how to obtain the -- the proposal and the decision. You haven't discussed that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No, we'll try to work it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. And otherwise, perhaps a short written message through VWS to the witness might -- that might be a way of resolving the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think a request to the Republic of Serbia is the only way and that we won't get the document in under a week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore, of course, I was seeking whether there was any informal way. The witness said -- but let's -- if you'd discuss that and whatever suggestion you make, we'll seriously consider it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again at paragraph 18 of the statement you -- there's another fellow there referred to, the author of the book, Gafurr Elsani. Do you know who Gafurr Elsani is? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is he?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Gafurr Elsani is a member of the People's Movement of Kosovo. Otherwise, he was the editor of Zeri i Kosoves, that was published in Switzerland. It was a bulletin of the People's Movement for the Republic of Kosovo, the acronym being the NPOK.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What involvement did he have in the publication of the KLA communiques which are in that book? And in answering the question, please tell the Chamber how you know about it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot say that I know that he participated in the drafting and the contents of the communiques. What I -- what I do know, though, is that the communiques issued by the Kosovo Liberation Army were printed in the newspaper whose editor-in-chief he was. This is Zeri i Kosoves.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Earlier you referred to these documents appearing in a book in 1998. Paragraph 18 refers to this book published in March 2003, and that's the one that's attached to your statement. Is the March 2003 the same book, a different edition, or what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It is the same book but another edition. The first edition was published in March 1998 in Arau in Switzerland by the People's Movement of Kosovo, and it was printed in the Zeri i Kosoves. Later it saw several new editions, and the one that I see here is from 2003. I think that there were about 10.000 copies printed in France during 1999. The first edition was printed in Switzerland, and it had 3.000 copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you read it in its original edition in 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps not in March 1998, but in early April certainly. As soon as the book was published, we received it from abroad. I am quite good in reading Albanian. I read it. And after a certain while, we also translated the entire book and its contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you can turn to annex 2, which I hope we might have a number for it by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's 65 ter number 01988, and it's been assigned Exhibit Number P934.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll just display in Sanction the part on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you can turn to the page which has "7" at the bottom of it in the copy you have, Mr. Stijovic. And it refers to KLA zones.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if you just look at the paragraph where it says, "The KLA was planned as an integral part of the occupied territories," and refers specifically to communiques 40 and 41 and says: "The KLA was operating in more than one zones, which were the zones ... " And then it explains the zones: One, two, three, four, five. Now, this is in the foreword to the book written by Mr. Dzemailji, described as the chairman of the LPK. My question is: How does the information in the foreword to the book and, of course, the communiques you referred to accord with the information your service had in 1998 or before about those five KLA territorial zones?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: There is something that I wanted to explain before giving an answer to your question. I believe it is important. There is a history to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the relevance to the -- the question. Is it a long explanation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'll try to limit my answer to what you asked me. In 1993, we arrested a group, a larger group of NPK members. Through the procedure they underwent, in terms of investigation and proceedings, we gained information on the plans and activities of the People's Movement of Kosovo. Later on, through various minutes of meetings, we came to learn that the People's Movement of Kosovo, which was still proclaiming its political goal as that of being an extremist goal, trying to unite all Albanian territories in the Balkans, and based on all that, we learned that they distributed -- or rather, divided the entire area in the Balkans populated by Albanians in five zones. The first one was in Kosovo, the second one in Macedonia, the third was in Serbia proper, in southern Serbia in Presevo, Bujanovac, and Medvedja. The fourth zone was in Montenegro, and the fifth was supposed to encompass certain activities in the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To assist you in where I'm going, I'm interesting in establishing the accuracy or otherwise of the KLA communiques in that book and your knowledge independently of the content of those communiques and the accuracy of the information provided in the foreword by Mr. Dzemailji and how he would have known to put the information about the five zones in the book. That's where I'm going. Does that assist you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, based on what I just said to you, how accurate, if you can answer that -- or how does what Mr. Dzemailji wrote about the zones accord with your own information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It is fully consistent. It fully accords with what we knew at that point in time about the level of organisation and plans for development of the NPK and KLA in the following period.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next paragraph is paragraph 19, where you refer to the KLA's first claim of responsibility for a terrorist act in a communique published on the 29th of November, 1994. Now, that's annex 3. And what I want to ask you is: Did you see that at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before I go on, can that also be given whatever the next number will be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's 65 ter number 01989, and I understand been marked for identification as P935.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of the -- what you called terrorist attack on a DB officer called Lutfi Ajazi at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Based on your information, is what is recorded in that particular publication, that is, of the 29th of November, 1994, accurate or not accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please turn to paragraph 20 of your statement in which you refer to -- before you do, I'll just go back to that other issue. Lutfi Ajazi, how did you know about -- did you know that person and how did you know about the attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Lutfi Ajazi is a colleague of mine, an operative of the DB who lived in Glogovac and worked in Pristina centre. We were together that entire day. And in the late evening hours, he went home. And after he spent some time in a bar in Glogovac, as he was driving back home in the late evening hours, some 100 to 150 metres from his home three unidentified persons attacked him, gravely wounding him. Two bullets hit him, one in the back and one in his knee. I learned of the attack five minutes after that, because his brother called me on the mobile and informed me that an attack had been carried out, that the family members returned fire - meaning his brother and his father opened fire from rifles - police came, and an ambulance took Lutfi to the hospital in Pristina. His relatives informed me about that. They wanted me to meet up with Lutfi in the hospital to see what treatment he would receive, and I did that. After he was admitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I stop you there. I think Mr. Re was mainly seeking what was the source of your personal knowledge on the matter, not further details, because I see that there are a lot of other events. If -- if we would go into details of all of them -- I mean, it's mainly a matter of Mr. Re seeking to establish that it's not just that you read something but that you have some personal knowledge which is in accordance with what is in the document. That's what he's mainly seeking. Please proceed, Mr. Re. And you are invited to -- to -- to explain such things to the witness and to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Moving to the next three years, 1995, 1996, and 1997, to which you refer in paragraph 20 of your statement, which we'll display in Sanction there, you refer to: "A dramatic increase in terrorist attacks against police and against Albanians ... " Now, you say you tracked the attack against the security forces and the civilian population in Kosovo from 1992 until 1998, and you subsequently reconstructed the figures. And the figures you've put there state eight attacks in 1992; 75 attacks in 1997; and 1.486 attacks through the 30th of November 1998. In the third paragraph of your statement, you also refer to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Re, are you saying 1998, November. It was not so clear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To make it clear, 1.486 attacks through the 30th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Paragraph 62, you also refer to a tabulation of those particular attacks. Now, the Trial Chamber is interested in how you have calculated those figures. And I'd like as brief an explanation as possible about the source of your information and how you did it. And I may have to -- please look at me, because I might stop you at -- once you start.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, these -- this is internal information available to the RDB. We, as the analysis department, analyse the events out in the field. And one of the elements we followed related to the terrorist events. And it was clearly registered that there was an escalation starting in late 1995. They were militarising and stepping up terrorist activities. And you can see that based on the figures. This is the information that came to our office, to the RDB. It was registered by the Ministry of the Interior, public security service, and information reported by the media. Later on, after 1999, I reconstructed these figures. I used some documents. First of all, the publication of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia called Bezbednost, meaning "security," which published these figures, and these figures were consistent with what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you define in compiling these figures as an attack? I mean, what constituted an attack to make it into this table?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: There are several theories to explain a terrorist attack. A terrorist attack, as defined by all services in the world --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- what I mean -- what I'm really interested in: Are we talking about assaults? Kidnappings? Murders? Hand-grenades? Threatening letters? Whatever. Just -- if you could just tell us the categories as defined by you in compiling these figures.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Attacks by firearms, hand-grenades and other explosives, attacks against citizens, Albanians, Serbs, MUP members, and members of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So based on -- are they based on police reports or what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Based on police reports, complaints, media reports, because these events were covered by the media both in Serbian and in Albanian. And one can easily establish this by looking at media reports from that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In degrees of serious, I want you to explain to the Trial Chamber what was the most -- what was the least serious which you included as an attack and what was the most serious type of event.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: The gravest attacks were those that were carried out with the use of firearms, hand-grenades, by planting explosive devices. Those were the most serious attacks or assaults, leading to murder and grave injury. Also assaults where fire was opened on the police, citizens, and the army without any consequences. I'm not dealing with the consequences of these attacks but the most serious attacks were the ones where firearms, hand-grenades, or explosives were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the threshold to make it to an attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In your table, what was the -- what was the level of seriousness that enabled you to classify it as a terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Active use of firearms, hand-grenades, explosive devices, regardless of the consequences that ensued. Attacks against the categories that I mentioned earlier: Citizens, MUP members, and members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. So from this table, can we exclude things such as threatening letters or threatening telephone calls or assaults with fists, those sorts of activities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry, because I -- I'm obviously anxious not to interrupt. But the witness refers to reconstructing figures based on a statistical survey in a magazine. I wonder if -- if we could just have clarification of what that process means. This is page 73, line 5. It's also in both paragraphs of the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, in view of, I would say, the explanation in the motion on this point, could you please seek to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Explain the process of and what you mean by "reconstruction."

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: "Reconstruction" means subsequent explanation of these events and analysis of these events. Attacks took place and were registered separately outside of the central records, if I can call them that. They were registered by police, by the army who had been attacked, and also by the media. Based on these three categories of data that appeared and that I managed to gather and also based on this magazine, which is a periodical of the Ministry of the Interior, I made a survey of these attacks that had been carried out during that period of time because we wanted to establish when these activities had escalated and had become much more intense. Essentially, there are no great differences. And if you were to compare the data published by the media - and by media I'm referring both to Albanian and Serbian media - you would see there's no difference between them and those registered by the military. The military focused on the attacks and illegal crossings of the border. The police focused mostly on the attacks against citizens and other types of attacks. And the media focused on all of these events. And by comparing them and conducting a comparative analysis, you would see that this information is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've mentioned three sources: Police, army, and media. Dealing with them one by one; police, just please tell us briefly what your sources of information were within the police. I mean, was it criminal records? Attacks? Reports? Or what? Then I'll come to the other two.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior comprises public security and state security. Public security deals with public law and order. They compile daily reports of events in Kosovo and Metohija. We would receive from the police on a daily basis this report on daily events in the territory. In addition to that, within the State Security Service, our operatives in the field also reported about the events, providing information on possible perpetrators of these events. This is as far as the police is concerned. As for the army --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Now, were statistics kept within the MUP of these terrorist attacks you've described?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. By analysing this data, one could draw important conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were the statistics kept on a yearly, weekly, or monthly basis? On what basis were they kept?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: There were several kinds of different methods that we used, statistical methods. At the regional level, based on the location of attacks, we conducted analysis both in terms of territory and in terms of time frame. Statistics also identified the kind of weapons and ammunition most frequently used in the attacks. And this statistical data pointed very clearly to the hot spots of activities of the KLA, places where their activities were most important.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these statistics published regularly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who -- who collected them?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: They were collected by the public security sector of the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia. They applied statistical methods, such as graphs, in order to illustrate clearly these events and attacks, and in addition to that, they also provided descriptions where they chronologically informed about what had happened, where, and the consequences of that. That was periodically published definitely every three months, every six months, and annually.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that in both public and security sectors, or did they do them -- did they do it separately or together or what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: We worked separately. Public security sector was mostly interested in data on that, and we used the public security data - that is to say, their analyses, their reports - in order to give a descriptive explanation of an event aimed at identifying the persons behind the attack or the event. And you can see it with breakdown of various other types of information which was announced at various press conferences of the MUP. You can also see that there were numerous analyses carried out in 1998 and 1999, and they were all pointing to this increasing danger stemming from the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you distinguish these terrorist attacks from non-terrorist attacks involving violence or extreme violence? And in saying that, I mean in compiling your report or your statistics.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: The message sent by terrorist attacks was a political one. The objective of those attacks was clear. They were meant to spread fear and insecurity among the public. Further, what is also important is a method of -- used in these terrorist acts. What is the key element here is that these attacks were carried out in a covert way from an ambush, close to people's homes by using firearms, hand-grenades, and explosive devices. In addition to that, what is a specific feature of terrorist attacks during this period of time is that they were not selective in the targets of their attacks. They attacked not only police and the army but also citizens, civilians, and they attacked them in the same way, covertly, from an ambush, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm looking at -- what I'm interested in is how did you or the police department or the MUP or whatever distinguish those terrorist attacks from other murders or acts of violence for the purposes of compiling these statistics? I mean, were statistics kept separately of terrorist attacks? If so, how did they distinguish a terrorist attack from a -- another type of murder?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. After these initial attacks in 1994 and 1995, every other attack was followed by a communique of the KLA, who took responsibility for the attack. And this was done in relation to each attack. This data is reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why was it reliable? I mean, was a comparison made between what the KLA were saying and the information the police had? I mean, tell the Trial Chamber why it was reliable.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I consider this information reliable because it is fully consistent with events on the ground. The sources of this information are mostly the media in the Albanian language. They would issue announcements or communiques in which they took responsibility for the events that had happened earlier on the ground; that is to say, murders, attacks, planting of explosive devices, hand-grenades, and so on. They published this in all types of media in the Albanian language, and it was later carried by other media houses, and they would invariably always announce these attacks subsequently and take responsibility for them. In these attacks, people were killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, may I just interrupt for one second. I -- I noticed that in the Defence motion that as far as these kind of communiques are concerned, that it's often said that the Defence doesn't oppose admission but, I suppose, not to admit to the authenticity or to the content. Now, if there would be any specific challenges to the authenticity of these documents of any specific nature, of course, the Chamber would very much like to hear such a --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not anticipating on what our decisions would be, but it struck me that it's repeated again and again --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that not admitting to its authenticity. If there are any specific authenticity concerns, the Chamber would like to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour will recall that this is the second witness who's given evidence with KLA communiques and in each --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, at this moment, I'm not seeking to have any further argument on the matter. Just to say that if you have any more specifics, any positive challenge to the authenticity, that we'd like to hear that at -- at a suitable moment. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Just to make sure that -- that we're clear. Is that authenticity to the document itself or authenticity to the information contained therein?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. There's a clear distinction made in the motion filed by Mr. Emmerson between authenticity of the document and the -- the -- whether the events described in the document really took place. I think I follow your language and -- which is just the document and nothing else at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, there's -- but there's also, I think, another -- a corollary issue, which is that the -- the document in which the communique is expressed is oftentimes a newspaper publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: So that take us one step away from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, whether you challenge whether it was published in a newspaper or not or whether this was the communique as was sent to the -- I mean, that's all about authenticity --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of either the publication itself or predecessor, it depends on how it was published. Sometimes it says, "We received this, we now publish it." But if there are any specific concerns on that, that's the -- then the Chamber would like to learn what the specific concerns are, rather than a general challenge to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- authenticity, yes. Please proceed. I take this point, Mr. Re, because were now dealing with this kind of document, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've dealt with the police. The second source was army. As briefly as you possibly can, what were your sources within the military? In -- in categories or statistics or whatever.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the military in Kosovo and Metohija, we had their information on the events first and foremost in the border belt towards Albania, concerning attacks and contraband of weapons and equipment. They forwarded that in written form as well as in the form of statistics. In addition to that, there was a small number of attacks on the members of the army and its facilities within the territory of Kosovo as well. We used that information first and foremost to cross-reference that information with what we know -- knew about the channels of introducing terrorists and weapons in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How was the information collected? I mean, in what form was it collected by the military? Was it in the form of reports or statistics or -- or what?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Depending on the circumstances and the time period. As their activities escalated, the army usually held press conferences through their press officers and they made public the events at the border, and then the state organs followed that up with diplomatic activities and acquainting the International Community with what was going on at the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did the army keep statistics of what you've called "terrorist attacks" in that period you've described, 1992 through 1998? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have access to those statistics?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you use those statistics in compiling your report you refer to in paragraph 20?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Next question: Which section of the army compiled or maintained their statistics?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It was done territorially by the brigades responsible for -- given zones of responsibility -- of responsibilities. It all went to the services of the corps and the military security service, which dealt with that data in professional terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying the military security service had a -- was a central repository for these -- for this data?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Is that where you got the information from?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: First and foremost, about the events in the border belt and the events in the territory of Kosovo that had to do with the military and its facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, is that "yes"?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, the third category was media. Before you answer, is there anything you can tell us about media sources you used in the report you referred to in paragraph 20 that you haven't already told us?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I -- just before the witness answers, Mr. Re has now made a number of references and questions to "the report you compiled that you refer to in paragraph 20." When I -- when I rose to my feet earlier on in relation to clarification of "reconstruction"," the reason is because in paragraph 20 the witness says he reconstructed the figures based on a magazine article in a MUP magazine and because in paragraph 62 he says "the statistical summary is based on information published in an official MUP magazine." Now, it may be that there is some separate report that this witness produced, but we certainly haven't seen it and it's not referred to, as Mr. Re suggests it is in terms, in paragraph 20 or in paragraph 62. So the clarification I am seeking is whether the statistics that are here put forward are the statistics that this witness has reconstructed, whatever that means, from a magazine article that he's read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Maybe I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When I said "report," did you do a report or are you only referring to a -- your own reconstruction for whatever purpose?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: While I was at the position of the head of analysis, we conducted detailed analysis using statistical methods in order to monitor the number of terrorist attacks. So as to respond specifically, I carried them over from various -- from the magazine called "Security" issued by the Ministry of the Interior. It -- it was the place that was the focus of -- the gathering of all information from the police, the military, and the media, and I believe that data was the most accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let's try to keep matters simple. Now, are these data as we find them here, are these data mainly taken from this publication or did you do all the work yourself and then at the end you were surprised that these figures were exactly or almost exactly the same as the statistics you compiled? It's -- it's a rather simple question. I mean, how many intellectual work was done by you and how much copying was done -- was involved? And now, which of the two is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very little. I copied most of it from what had already been printed, accessible to the public, and that is what I based it on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I understand. And we therefore -- reconstruction -- I mean, copying and reconstructing is not exactly the same. Did you -- while copying, did you look at it and adopt them as being reliable, or did you do any further -- did you further elaborate on the -- or did you just accept them as -- as reliable information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I compared that to the reports printed in the media, and the military had their reports. By using all that, I arrived at the conclusion that the figure was as such. It did not vary much in terms of percentage and it could be a sound basis to assess the events in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "it didn't differ much." Was it exactly the same or was it almost the same or -- or was it exactly the same? I gave you two options: Exactly or almost.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, practically the same, since in those attacks many of them that took place in the border belt were not shown. At a certain moment, certain bodies qualified those attacks differently. Therefore, using -- if -- had I used all the data that was available, this -- these figures would have been far greater. But I tried to limit my answer, and in that regard, there is not much variation. Therefore, I thought it was relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are many words, but -- but perhaps one simple question: If we would have available the figures published in that magazine, in that MUP magazine, would we find any difference or would it be exactly the same?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Almost the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I do apologise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Almost exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see the time. It may be that I've misunderstood, but my understanding is that the figures we see in the 92 ter statement have been taken from the magazine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If that's wrong --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, from your motion, I think you use the word "just copied from".

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore, Mr. Re, you -- let's get to the core of the case right away. Are we meeting very much a coincidence that the intellectual work of two independently operating entities result in exactly the same numbers, 1486, or is there any other explanation for that? That is -- Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only reason I'm on my feet is that I noticed that the witness when he came into court had a nice juicy fat briefcase with him. It might be worth inquiring whether he actually has the -- the magazine articles with him that could perhaps resolve this one way or the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll ask him. We were talking a lot about the publication of statistical data in a MUP magazine. Would you happen to have a copy of that magazine with you at this moment or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't bring it. I think it's in my hotel. I -- where I have another issue of that magazine, and you can see something similar there, how the information was published by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you be willing to bring that if we continue your examination next week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then looking at the clock, Mr. Re, I think we have to adjourn for the -- not only for the day but also for the week. Mr. Stijovic, we have not finished yet, as you may have noticed. We will adjourn until Monday, the 8th of October, at quarter past 2.00 in Courtroom II, which is a different courtroom. But before I let you go, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about the testimony already given or still to be given. There might be one little exception, that is, if you receive a written message - I say "if." I do not know whether you will receive it - a written message to inquire into the availability of the proposal and the decision on the operation - what was it? - Circle, I think, Krug, then, of course, you're entitled. But then limited to that subject only to get in touch with those who could provide a -- copies of that material. But whether we will ask you or not is still uncertain. With apologies to interpreters and technicians, we adjourn until the 8th of October, quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
